_comment: Well-known ports and why finding them open on an arbitrary public host is interesting. 'risk' is a baseline; derive_findings adjusts it with banner/TLS evidence.

21.name: FTP
21.note: Unencrypted file transfer; check for anonymous login

22.name: SSH
22.note: Remote admin; note the banner version

23.name: Telnet
23.note: Unencrypted remote admin, commonly default-credentialed on IoT/embedded gear

25.name: SMTP
25.note: Mail transfer; check for open relay behaviour separately

53.name: DNS
53.note: Open resolver if it answers recursive queries from the internet

111.name: RPCbind
111.note: Legacy ONC RPC portmapper, frequently abused for NFS/amplification

123.name: NTP
123.note: Time sync; monlist-capable servers are abused for amplification

135.name: MSRPC
135.note: Windows RPC endpoint mapper exposed to the internet

161.name: SNMP
161.note: Often left on default community strings ('public'); also DDoS-amplification vector

443.name: HTTPS
443.note: Web service over TLS; see TLS cert findings

445.name: SMB
445.note: Windows file sharing exposed to the internet, historically mass-exploited (WannaCry/EternalBlue class)

631.name: IPP/CUPS
631.note: Printing service; has had internet-facing RCE history

2049.name: NFS
2049.note: Network filesystem exposed to the internet

2375.name: Docker API
2375.note: Unauthenticated Docker daemon API gives remote code execution if reachable

3000.name: Dev server
3000.note: Common dev/admin app port (Grafana, Node, Rails) left exposed

3389.name: RDP
3389.note: Windows Remote Desktop exposed publicly, a top ransomware entry vector

5900.name: VNC
5900.note: Remote framebuffer access, frequently run with no or weak auth

6379.name: Redis
6379.note: In-memory datastore, historically shipped with no auth by default

7547.name: TR-069 CWMP
7547.note: ISP CPE remote-management protocol, repeatedly mass-exploited

8080.name: HTTP-alt/proxy
8080.note: Common secondary web or proxy port

8888.name: HTTP-alt
8888.note: Common dev/notebook port (e.g. Jupyter) left exposed

9000.name: HTTP-alt/PHP-FPM
9000.note: Frequently an app admin port or PHP-FPM exposed to the internet

9200.name: Elasticsearch
9200.note: Search/datastore API, historically found wide open with full data access

11211.name: Memcached
11211.note: No-auth cache service, a well-known massive DDoS-amplification vector

27017.name: MongoDB
27017.note: Database engine, long history of unauthenticated internet-facing instances
